claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: the claim text now matches the round-1 suggested_text. Traefik v3.7 Kubernetes setup page: "helm repo add traefik https://traefik.github.io/charts" and "We use the official Traefik Helm chart for a managed and customizable installation."; v3.7 docs home: "Traefik is an open-source Application Proxy". apps/traefik.yaml lines 13-14 hold that repoURL and chart.

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Helm v3 Chart Repository Guide: "A chart repository is an HTTP server that houses an index.yaml file and optionally some packaged charts." Helm v3 Charts topic: "Packages in repositories are identified by name plus version."

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Helm v3 Charts topic, Chart.yaml fields: "version: The version of the chart (required)"; "appVersion: The version of the app that this contains (optional)." and "Note that the appVersion field is not related to the version field."

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/traefik-install.txt lines 40 and 42: "1 < image: docker.io/traefik:v3.7.12" / "1 > image: docker.io/traefik:v3.7.13" for renders of 41.4.0 and 41.6.1. appVersion v3.7.13 for chart 41.6.1 recorded in content/versions.yaml (traefik key).

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Argo CD 3.1 Helm guide: "Argo CD supports the equivalent of a values file directly in the Application manifest", example under source.helm.valuesObject.

helm show values: "displays the contents of the values.yaml file"; --version, --repo flags (round 1). Round 2, for the added naming part: helm install lists "By chart reference: helm install mymaria example/mariadb" and "By chart reference and repo url: helm install --repo https://example.com/charts/ mynginx nginx"; Traefik setup page: "helm repo add traefik https://traefik.github.io/charts". So traefik/traefik and traefik --repo <url> name the same chart.
Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Argo CD 3.1 Helm guide: "Helm is only used to inflate charts with helm template" and "The lifecycle of the application is handled by Argo CD instead of Helm."

Carried from round 1. Argo CD Helm guide: "Helm is only used to inflate charts with helm template". Output stage-3 lines 33-34: "$ helm list --all-namespaces" followed only by the header line.

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). The only path: entries in deploy/gitops/config-repo/apps/*.yaml are envs/staging, platform/edge, platform/policies; none syncs apps/. traefik-install.sh applies apps/traefik.yaml with kubectl; captured output line 15: "$ kubectl apply -f .gitops/donhang-config/apps/traefik.yaml".

apps/traefik.yaml: valuesObject sets five leaf values: providers.kubernetesGateway.enabled (24), gateway.enabled false (27, comment line 25 "No Gateway from the chart: Đơn Hàng writes its own"), service.spec.type NodePort (32), ports.web.nodePort 30080 (35), ports.websecure.nodePort 30443 (37); comment 28-29 "the staging node publishes these two ports on the host"; automated selfHeal/prune 42-44, syncOptions 47-49.

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Helm v3 Values Files: "values.yaml is the default, which can be overridden by a parent chart's values.yaml, which can in turn be overridden by a user-supplied values file"; "Helm will coalesce the default and overridden keys together".

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Output stage-3 line 36: "== helm show values: 56 top-level keys, 1697 lines", from the echo with grep -c '^[a-zA-Z]' and wc -l over helm show values ... --version 41.6.1.

Round 2: the claim was reworded as suggested. helm template: "Render chart templates locally and display the output." "Any values that would normally be looked up or retrieved in-cluster will be faked locally." No release: Argo CD renders with helm template and helm list prints only its header (claim 9). kubectl --dry-run: "If client strategy, only print the object that would be sent, without sending it."

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Output stage-3 lines 38-42: "8 < helm.sh/chart: traefik-41.4.0", "1 < image: docker.io/traefik:v3.7.12", "8 > helm.sh/chart: traefik-41.6.1", "1 > image: docker.io/traefik:v3.7.13" from diff <(render 41.4.0) <(render 41.6.1) | ... | uniq -c.

Ingress provider still on: valuesObject does not touch providers.kubernetesIngress, and at stage-3 Traefik routes an Ingress: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/ingress.txt "HTTP 404" before and "HTTP 200" after applying api-ingress.yaml; traefik-install.txt line 30: gatewayclass traefik ACCEPTED True.

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Argo CD 3.1 Automated Sync Policy, Automatic Self-Healing: "By default, changes that are made to the live cluster will not trigger automated sync." Self-heal enables "automatic sync when the live cluster's state deviates from the state defined in Git". apps/traefik.yaml sets selfHeal: true.

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Helm v3 Values Files: "values.yaml is the default ... which can in turn be overridden by a user-supplied values file". A copied key is user-supplied, so it overrides whatever default a newer chart version ships.

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). Opinion stated with its condition (reviewers need to see what Đơn Hàng changes) and with the counter-case (a full copy shows every value), in section 6; not presented as an unconditional rule.

New in round 2. Argo CD 3.1 Declarative Setup: the Application is "the Kubernetes resource object representing a deployed application instance"; manifests "can be updated using kubectl apply"; example: "kubectl apply -n argocd -f application.yaml". With no Application syncing apps/ (claim 10), a Git commit to apps/traefik.yaml does not reach that object until the file is applied again.

Carried from round 1 (claim unchanged). traefik-install.sh @ stage-3 line 7: helm() { command helm --kube-context kind-donhang-staging "$@"; }; line 8: show() { echo "\$ $*"; "$@"; }; line 10: chart_repo=https://traefik.github.io/charts.

New in round 2. git-revert DESCRIPTION: "Given one or more existing commits, revert the changes that the related patches introduce, and record some new commits that record them." issues.text: Carried from round 1. Several shell pieces are still not explained: `command helm` (why not just helm), `<( … )` inside diff, `|| true`, and `$config_repo` (the prose explains only `chart_repo`). I can follow the idea from the prose, but not the line.
issues.quote: diff <(render 41.4.0) <(render 41.6.1) | grep '^[<>]' | sed -E 's/^([<>]) +/\1 /' | sort | uniq -c || true
issues.fix: Add one sentence to the prose under the output: "`<(render …)` hands each render to diff as if it were a file, `|| true` keeps the script going because diff exits with an error when it finds differences, and `$config_repo` is the local copy of the config repository."

issues.text: New in the rewritten paragraph. 'Routing object' now names two things: the second kind Traefik follows besides its default, and the one the chart would create. I cannot tell whether the object the chart would create is of the first or the second kind. Not needed for the main idea.
issues.quote: They stop the chart from creating a routing object of its own, because Đơn Hàng writes its own in a later lesson
issues.fix: Say which kind: 'creating a routing object of the second kind of its own', or name it with the same word the YAML comment uses.

issues.text: New in the rewritten paragraph. The paragraph under the YAML now does six things (two numbers, where the chart comes from, `traefik/traefik`, the shown value, the four hidden values, sync). I had to read it twice.
issues.quote: `repoURL` and `chart` say where the chart comes from; the comment's `traefik/traefik` is the same chart as `traefik --repo <chart repository>` in the script.
